benchmarks.label: Average global breach cost · 2025
benchmarks.description: Global mean in IBM’s 2025 study of 600 breached organisations, covering March 2024 to February 2025. Historical benchmark, not a Cyberonik result or your expected loss.

benchmarks.label: Identify-and-contain lifecycle · 2025
benchmarks.description: Global mean breach lifecycle in IBM’s 2025 study. This combines identification and containment; it is not continuous downtime or a service response target.

benchmarks.label: Expect AI to reshape cybersecurity · 2026
benchmarks.description: Share of WEF respondents who anticipated AI as the biggest driver of cybersecurity change in 2026. The survey covered 804 qualified participants across 92 countries; this measures expectations, not attack growth.

benchmarks.label: Higher cost with extensive shadow AI · 2025
benchmarks.description: Average breach-cost difference between high and low or no shadow-AI use in IBM’s 2025 study. An observed comparison, not a forecast for your organisation.

benchmarks.label: Lower cost with extensive security AI · 2025
benchmarks.description: Extensive security AI and automation users had lower mean breach costs and an 80-day shorter lifecycle than non-users in IBM’s 2025 study. The association does not establish AI alone caused the difference.

benchmarks.label: Reported rising fraud and phishing · 2025
benchmarks.description: Share of WEF respondents who perceived more cyber-enabled fraud and phishing during 2025. This is a survey perception, not a 77% increase in measured attack volume.

benchmarks.label: Average global breach cost · 2026
benchmarks.description: Global mean in IBM’s 2026 study of 602 organisations breached between March 2025 and February 2026. An annual research benchmark, not a live loss counter or your expected loss.

benchmarks.label: Internet-crime losses reported to IC3 · 2025
benchmarks.description: Losses in complaints received by FBI IC3 during 2025, rounded as in the annual report. This is not all worldwide cybercrime, not businesses only and not a live counter.

benchmarks.label: Business email compromise losses · 2025
benchmarks.description: US$3,046,598,558 in losses reported to FBI IC3 under business email compromise during 2025. Included within IC3’s overall reported-loss total; do not add it again.

benchmarks.label: Losses in complaints referencing AI · 2025
benchmarks.description: US$893,346,472 in reported IC3 losses carrying an AI-related descriptor. This category overlaps crime types and the overall total; it is not a separate sum or a count of proven AI-caused breaches.
